new_entities.name: Phosphatidylserine supplementation
new_entities.description: Oral phosphatidylserine supplementation used to support membrane function and stress resilience.

new_entities.name: Exercise-induced cortisol response
new_entities.description: Acute cortisol response to physical or exercise-related stress.

edges.population: healthy active men exposed to exercise or stress-testing protocols
edges.mechanism: Phosphatidylserine has been proposed to damp hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal activation during repeated physical stress, possibly by altering cell-signaling dynamics or membrane-related neuroendocrine responses. The small human dataset is inconsistent, however, with one direct exercise study showing a lower cortisol area-under-the-curve and other related phospholipid stress studies showing no meaningful cortisol attenuation.
edges.summary: Claims that phosphatidylserine reliably blunts exercise-induced cortisol are not settled. One small crossover trial reported a substantially lower cortisol response during moderate-intensity exercise, but another exercise study found no significant effect on serum cortisol, and a phospholipid stress trial outside the exercise setting also failed to show salivary-cortisol attenuation.
edges.caveats: This edge rests on very small human studies with different formulations, exercise protocols, and stress paradigms. It is better treated as an unsettled sports-endocrine hypothesis than a dependable cortisol-lowering strategy.

evidence.citation: Starks MA et al 2008 J Int Soc Sports Nutr
evidence.notes: The effects of phosphatidylserine on endocrine response to moderate intensity exercise.

effect_quant.comparator: phosphatidylserine versus placebo for cortisol area under the curve during exercise testing
